speaker: Unknown
en: Good to go.
zh: 准备好了。

speaker: Unknown
en: All right.
zh: 好的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, take a quick sip and then let's start.
zh: 嗯，快喝一口然后我们开始吧。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is great to be here.
zh: 很高兴来到这里。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is like my third year coming to this conference and I always really enjoy it.
zh: 这大概是我第三年来参加这个会议了，我一直都很享受它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And thank you for coming to this workshop.
zh: 感谢大家来参加这个研讨会。

speaker: Unknown
en: I know there's many interesting talks.
zh: 我知道有很多精彩的演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: Let me talk a little bit about our view of asynchronous agents at Anthropic and some things we've been up to lately.
zh: 让我谈谈 Anthropic 对异步智能体的一些看法，以及我们最近在做的一些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is kind of a way I think about models and product.
zh: 所以这大概是我思考模型和产品的一种方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you can think about Cloud as a light source, and you can think about products as windows that allow the light to pass through.
zh: 你可以把 Cloud 看作光源，把产品看作允许光线通过的窗户。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what's kind of interesting is over time, the window that you need to actually kind of see the light of the model kind of shifts.
zh: 有趣的是，随着时间的推移，你实际需要的用来看到模型光芒的窗户会发生转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've seen this over the past few years.
zh: 我们在过去几年里已经看到了这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I'm plotting here different Cloud models and their task horizon.
zh: 所以我在这里绘制了不同的 Cloud 模型及其任务视界。

speaker: Unknown
en: So how much autonomous work can they do over time?
zh: 也就是它们随着时间的推移能做多少自主工作？

speaker: Unknown
en: And you might recall back in the Opus 3 days, this was kind of like 2024, models could only do maybe 10 to 20 minutes of autonomous work.
zh: 你可能回想起来，在 Opus 3 时代，这大概是在 2024 年，模型只能做大概 10 到 20 分钟的自主工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is measured by meter.
zh: 这是通过 meter 测量的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And in that regime, only certain product surfaces made sense.
zh: 在那个阶段，只有某些产品形态才有意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Things like autocomplete, things like chat, where your human is very in the loop.
zh: 比如自动补全，比如聊天，其中人类需要深度参与其中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because the model's really only doing a very short amount of work before you're steering it.
zh: 因为模型实际上只做非常短的工作，然后你就需要引导它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now the past year we saw the rise of synchronous coding agents like Cloud Code and this is kind of a shift because then models could do maybe an hour of work.
zh: 在过去一年，我们看到了同步编码智能体如 Cloud Code 的兴起，这是一种转变，因为那时模型大概可以做一小时的工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it made sense to have them run but typically locally where you could still steer them easily.
zh: 所以让它们运行是有意义的，但通常是在本地，这样你仍然可以轻松地引导它们。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it's kind of interesting because during this regime I remember efforts and I was involved in some efforts to build kind of asynchronous agents.
zh: 这很有趣，因为在这个阶段，我记得有一些努力，我也参与了一些努力来构建某种异步智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: But when models can only do like an hour of work, async as an experience is kind of bad.
zh: 但是当模型只能做大约一小时的工作时，异步作为一种体验是很糟糕的。

speaker: Unknown
en: The model goes off and it like hits an error and it comes back to you over a short period of time.
zh: 智能体跑出去，遇到错误，然后在很短的时间内回来找你。

speaker: Unknown
en: In order to really unlock async, we needed longer task horizons.
zh: 为了真正解锁异步，我们需要更长的任务视界。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so we're starting to see that now.
zh: 而我们现在开始看到这一点了。

speaker: Unknown
en: And kind of with this shift in capability and time horizon came a shift in the API surfaces.
zh: 随着这种能力和时间视界的转变，API 界面也发生了转变。

speaker: Unknown
en: So if you look at the lower left,
zh: 所以如果你看左下角，

speaker: Unknown
en: Message API came out like two years ago.
zh: Messages API 是大约两年前发布的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's basically prompt response.
zh: 它基本上是提示响应。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's great for building harnesses, but it's a very simple API.
zh: 它非常适合构建 harness，但它是一个非常简单的 API。

speaker: Unknown
en: Again, you're just passing inside messages, you get a response out.
zh: 同样，你只是传入消息，得到响应。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no sense of deployment with that.
zh: 它没有部署的概念。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you basically take messages API and you can roll your own harness.
zh: 所以你基本上拿 Messages API，你可以构建你自己的 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: You can deploy that harness and you have an agent.
zh: 你可以部署那个 harness，你就有一个智能体了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now over the past year, we saw the rise of coding agents in particular.
zh: 在过去一年，我们看到了编码智能体的兴起。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we released agent SDK.
zh: 所以我们发布了 agent SDK。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that's basically a way to programmatically call cloud code.
zh: 这基本上是一种以编程方式调用 cloud code 的方式。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's basically us giving you a harness.
zh: 这基本上是我们给你一个 harness。

speaker: Unknown
en: But over the past few months since April, as we've seen longer and longer task horizons, we released a new APL called Managed Agents, which basically packages both the harness as well as all the managed deployment infrastructure for you.
zh: 但在过去几个月，从四月开始，随着我们看到越来越长的任务视界，我们发布了一个新的 APL，叫做 Managed Agents，它基本上为你打包了 harness 以及所有受管理的部署基础设施。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'll talk about some of the themes that underpin this new surface, Cloud Managed Agents, and some of the themes that...
zh: 我将谈谈支撑这个新界面 Cloud Managed Agents 的一些主题，以及一些主题……

speaker: Unknown
en: kind of extend beyond just managed agents broadly to think about this kind of new type of asynchronous agents, which can apply, of course, to clause and other types of kind of longer running long horizon agents.
zh: 延伸到不仅仅是受管理的智能体，广泛地思考这种新型的异步智能体，这当然适用于 clause 和其他类型的长期运行的长视界智能体。

speaker: Unknown
en: So theme one is decoupling the brain from the hands.
zh: 所以第一个主题是将大脑与手解耦。

speaker: Unknown
en: So when we first set out to build managed agents, we started with the container.
zh: 所以当我们最初开始构建受管理的智能体时，我们从容器开始。

speaker: Unknown
en: We put the harness in the sandbox in the same container.
zh: 我们把 harness 放在沙箱里的同一个容器中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, the problem here is what happens if the harness dies or the container dies?
zh: 现在，问题在于如果 harness 挂了或者容器挂了会发生什么？

speaker: Unknown
en: What we saw is we actually lose the session.
zh: 我们看到的是我们实际上丢失了会话。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, basically, this architecture is kind of tricky for long horizon agents because what can happen is your agent is running and if that container dies, you lose everything with it.
zh: 所以，基本上，这种架构对于长视界智能体来说有点棘手，因为可能发生的是你的智能体正在运行，如果那个容器挂了，你会失去所有东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: Also, as models get more capable, putting the credentials in the same container with the agent itself can be problematic.
zh: 此外，随着模型变得更有能力，将凭证放在与智能体本身相同的容器中可能会是有问题的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for example, giving Cloud access to a bunch of your secrets and letting it run for 10 hours and you're not watching it can be a little bit spooky and has some security concerns, especially as models get extremely capable.
zh: 所以，例如，给予 Cloud 对你的一堆秘密的访问权限并让它运行 10 个小时而你没有监视它，可能有点令人毛骨悚然，并且有一些安全问题，特别是随着模型变得非常有能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, for this reason, we kind of decouple what we call the brain, that's the harness from the hands, the execution environments, and Managed Agents is set up like this.
zh: 所以，因为这个原因，我们某种程度上解耦了我们所谓的“大脑”，也就是 harness，与“双手”，也就是执行环境，Managed Agents 就是这样设置的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the story here is that the harness becomes a stateless process.
zh: 这里的故事是，harness 变成了一个无状态进程。

speaker: Unknown
en: that talks to a session, the session is an append-only event log, and that can reach out to hands which are just containers.
zh: 它与一个会话对话，该会话是一个仅追加的事件日志，并且可以伸出手，也就是那些容器。

speaker: Unknown
en: So those are sandboxes, work is done.
zh: 所以这些是沙箱，工作是在那里完成的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one thing that's interesting is, Cloud is increasingly capable of managing many hands.
zh: 有趣的一件事是，Cloud 越来越有能力管理许多“双手”。

speaker: Unknown
en: So that is, you can give one harness access to many different containers to perform tool execution, and Cloud can manage this very easily and effectively.
zh: 也就是说，你可以给一个 harness 访问许多不同容器的权限来执行工具执行，而 Cloud 可以非常轻松且有效地管理这一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: If the session, sorry, if the harness dies or sandbox dies, it's completely fine because the session is always backed up in this append-only log and credentials are never actually added to the sandbox.
zh: 如果会话，抱歉，如果 harness 死了或者沙箱死了，这完全没问题，因为会话总是备份在这个仅追加的日志中，而且凭据实际上从未被添加到沙箱中。

speaker: Unknown
en: They're stored in a separate vault.
zh: 它们存储在一个独立的保险库中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So, this decoupling actually makes it quite reliable and safe, particularly for long horizon tasks.
zh: 所以，这种解耦实际上使其相当可靠且安全，特别是对于长期视野的任务。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is kind of one of the core ideas that underpins Managed Agents architecturally.
zh: 这可以说是架构上支撑 Managed Agents 的核心思想之一。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think an interesting thing that falls out of this is related to, you guys may have kind of seen or come across the recursive language models work, the session becomes an external context object that the model interrogates.
zh: 我认为由此产生的一个有趣的事情与你们可能看过或遇到的递归语言模型工作有关，即会话变成了模型查询的外部上下文对象。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this has all sorts of benefits for context management.
zh: 这对上下文管理有各种好处。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you think about it, when you're doing something like compaction, you're choosing some logic to retain some amount of context, and naively, in a kind of a typical step, you're discarding all the context that you didn't compact.
zh: 所以想一想，当你做诸如压缩之类的事情时，你选择某种逻辑来保留一定量的上下文，而且天真地，在一种典型的步骤中，你正在丢弃你没有压缩的所有上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: In this architecture, and also more broadly with recursive language models, the idea is that the context object is persistent and is unadulterated.
zh: 在这种架构中，以及更广泛地在递归语言模型中，其想法是上下文对象是持久的且未被篡改的。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's append only.
zh: 所以它是仅追加的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the model can always go back and fetch old context.
zh: 模型总是可以回溯并获取旧的上下文。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it basically creates a very, very nice architecture for context engineering because the core context object is immutable in the sense that it's non-destructive and you only append to it over time.
zh: 所以它基本上为上下文工程创造了一个非常好的架构，因为核心上下文对象在某种意义上是不可变的，即它是非破坏性的，你只是随着时间的推移向其追加内容。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've seen this to be quite nice in terms of long horizon context engineering as well.
zh: 所以我们发现这在长期视野的上下文工程方面也相当不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the second theme is use verifiers.
zh: 那么第二个主题是使用验证器。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the problems that we've seen with Claude and other models in general is that when you ask them to do a bunch of work and then say, okay, grade your work, if that same context is being used to both do the work and grade, you can get lots of odd artifacts and confabulation and basically odd behavior.
zh: 我们在 Claude 和其他模型上看到的一个问题是，当你要求它们做一堆工作然后说，好的，给你的工作打分，如果同样的上下文被用来既做工作又打分，你可能会得到许多奇怪的产物和幻觉，基本上就是奇怪的行为。

speaker: Unknown
en: For example, this is just an image showing you can think about that context window is filled with lots of different information and the model is grading itself.
zh: 例如，这只是一张图片，你可以想到上下文窗口里充满了许多不同的信息，模型正在给自己打分。

speaker: Unknown
en: Often it's not properly tuned to do kind of critical verification.
zh: 通常它没有经过适当的调整来进行那种批判性的验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so what we found is it's quite effective to separate verification into a separate context window.
zh: 所以我们发现，将验证分离到一个单独的上下文窗口中是相当有效的。

speaker: Unknown
en: This is a very general trend.
zh: 这是一个非常普遍的趋势。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about it in a number of different engineering blogs.
zh: 我们在许多不同的工程博客中谈论它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason is the verifier context can be tuned very specifically for the critique or verification task.
zh: 原因是验证器上下文可以非常专门地针对批评或验证任务进行调整。

speaker: Unknown
en: And so the way this works in practice is,
zh: 所以这在实践中是这样工作的，

speaker: Unknown
en: When you build loops, you can have a loop of a build context and a verifier context, and this can be a build agent, verifier agent, and what happens is the verifier has some goal or rubric, and it's verifying the result or work of the build agent, and this continues in a loop until verification is complete.
zh: 当你构建循环时，你可以有一个构建上下文和验证器上下文的循环，这可以是一个构建智能体、验证器智能体，发生的事情是验证器有一些目标或标准，它正在验证构建智能体的结果或工作，这在一个循环中持续进行，直到验证完成。

speaker: Unknown
en: And this is really the big idea behind this whole loops trend that you might have heard about, and we found to be kind of a very powerful paradigm, especially for working with some of the higher capacity models.
zh: 这实际上是你可能听说过的整个循环趋势背后的主要思想，我们发现这是一种非常强大的范式，特别是对于使用一些更高容量的模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: And here's some of the primitives.
zh: 这里有一些基元。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in Cloud Code, you have goal.
zh: 所以在 Cloud Code 中，你有 goal。

speaker: Unknown
en: In Managed Agents, you have outcomes.
zh: 在 Managed Agents 中，你有 outcomes。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the principles are really the same.
zh: 原则实际上是相同的。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're setting up a measurable end state in both cases.
zh: 在这两种情况下，你都在建立一个可测量的最终状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're using an independent context model.
zh: 你正在使用一个独立的上下文模型。

speaker: Unknown
en: You're using independent context to grade over the course of this loop.
zh: 你正在使用独立的上下文在这个循环过程中进行评分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The loop can run and you only exit the loop until this independent verifier has verified that it has the outcomes or outputs that you want.
zh: 循环可以运行，你只有在独立验证器验证了它具有你想要的结果或输出时才退出循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's the key idea.
zh: 这就是关键思想。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now let me tell you a story about how I've used this.
zh: 现在让我讲一个关于我如何使用它的故事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is a kind of a fun and interesting challenge called Parameter Golf.
zh: 所以这是一个有趣且有趣的挑战，叫做 Parameter Golf。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's a benchmark that was put up by OpenAI.
zh: 那是 OpenAI 发布的一个基准测试。

speaker: Unknown
en: And it tests model's ability to effectively do kind of ML research.
zh: 它测试模型有效地进行某种机器学习研究的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it asked the model to basically take a small kind of model and train it with eight H100 GPUs in less than 10 minutes.
zh: 它要求模型基本上拿一个小模型并在不到 10 分钟内用八个 H100 GPU 训练它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you see on the Y is basically you can think about it as loss, so lower is better, okay?
zh: 你在 Y 轴上看到的基本上可以认为是损失，所以越低越好，好吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And what I did was I set up a kind of a verifier loop using managed agents and outcomes.
zh: 我做的是我建立了一个使用 managed agents 和 outcomes 的验证器循环。

speaker: Unknown
en: to test the ability for Opus 4.7 and one of our frontier models, like mythos class models, on this task.
zh: 来测试 Opus 4.7 和我们的一个前沿模型，比如 mythos 级模型，在这个任务上的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what you see is, basically, I allow the model to continue to iterate until the outcome that I specify is satisfied, which is it finished exactly 20 iterations and it kind of met all the experimental criteria as defined by the benchmark.
zh: 你看到的是，基本上，我允许模型继续迭代，直到我指定的结果得到满足，即它恰好完成了 20 次迭代，并且它满足了基准定义的所有实验标准。

speaker: Unknown
en: What you see is the frontier capability models
zh: 你看到的是前沿能力模型

speaker: Unknown
en: are extremely good with this pattern of loops and verification.
zh: 非常擅长这种循环和验证模式。

speaker: Unknown
en: Because what happens is instead of encoding steering into me as the human, you're encoding the signal into the environment.
zh: 因为发生的事情是，与其将转向编码到我作为人类身上，不如将信号编码到环境中。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the model can self-correct when it receives feedback from, for example, the verifier.
zh: 所以当模型收到来自例如验证者的反馈时，它可以自我修正。

speaker: Unknown
en: And using this kind of paradigm with very high capacity models, you can get very strong results.
zh: 并且利用这种范式配合高容量模型，你可以得到非常强的结果。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the main point I'm trying to make here is that this paradigm of loops, which a lot of people have been talking about today, paired with very capacity models is a very good general primitive for long-running asynchronous work.
zh: 所以我在这里试图提出的主要观点是，这种很多人今天都在谈论的循环范式，配合高容量模型，是用于长时间运行的异步工作的一个非常好的通用原语。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's really the key point here.
zh: 这才是这里的关键点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now let me talk about another theme of self-learning.
zh: 现在让我谈谈自我学习的另一个主题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the human brain has two kind of interesting systems for memory.
zh: 所以人类大脑有两个非常有趣的记忆系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So one is, as you go about your day, the hippocampus is kind of writing traces of kind of short-term, very fast kind of experiential memory.
zh: 一个是，当你度过你的一天时，海马体基本上是在写入短期、非常快速的体验性记忆痕迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: Like, you might remember what you had for lunch today.
zh: 比如，你可能会记得你今天午饭吃了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: You had lunch an hour ago, you kind of remember.
zh: 你一小时前吃了午饭，你大概记得。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of written to short-term memory.
zh: 那就是写入了短期记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: When you go to bed at night, though, an offline process or out-of-band process dreams.
zh: 但是当你晚上睡觉时，一个离线过程或带外过程会做梦。

speaker: Unknown
en: And dreaming stores certain important details to long-term memory in the cortex.
zh: 并且做梦会将某些重要的细节存储到皮层中的长期记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: So for example, tomorrow, you might not remember what you ate for lunch today.
zh: 举个例子，明天，你可能不记得你今天午饭吃了什么。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of a local trace.
zh: 那是一种局部痕迹。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you had a very important experience today, maybe this talk, maybe not this talk.
zh: 但如果你今天有一次非常重要的经历，也许这次演讲，也许不是这次演讲。

speaker: Unknown
en: But if you had an interesting experience today, that might be written to long-term memory.
zh: 但如果你今天有一次有趣的经历，那可能会被写入长期记忆。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's kind of the point.
zh: 这就是重点。

speaker: Unknown
en: So these two subsystems in human work like this.
zh: 所以人类中的这两个子系统就是这样工作的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And we've actually found memory systems with Claude actually can employ these same two principles.
zh: 我们实际上发现 Claude 的记忆系统实际上可以采用同样的这两个原则。

speaker: Unknown
en: So this is showing Claude's capacity as an in-band memory writer.
zh: 这展示了 Claude 作为带内记忆写入者的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: So you basically give Claude memory tools.
zh: 所以你基本上给 Claude 记忆工具。

speaker: Unknown
en: And when I say memory tools, I mean it's basically the ability to write to a file system that is basically a memory directory.
zh: 当我说记忆工具时，我的意思是它基本上是写入文件系统的能力，该文件系统基本上是一个记忆目录。

speaker: Unknown
